limitations: Source-only PASS does not establish PostgreSQL replay, actual migration application, browser/UI accessibility, backend privileges at runtime, listener readiness, CI, deployment or live-database safety. Other workers execution reports are not promoted into this review.

Original SQL 1.0.0 accepted some plaintext that the application validator rejected. The new migration intentionally preserves that historical SQL behavior; stricter full plaintext parity is confined to the new 1.1.0 branch, avoiding reinterpretation of immutable old content.

Owner identity is accepted from the supplied trusted conversation provenance. Hash checks verify the recorded bytes, not independent speaker authentication or wall-clock acceptance-before-code chronology. The historical issue remains evidence of pre-promotion acceptance cases, not an activation grant.

The gate assumes the reviewed inspector and its external review digest trust anchor are trusted. Hashes detect drift; they are not a cryptographic signature or protection against an attacker replacing the gate itself. Local activation additionally requires the existing external exact-clean-tree attestation.

Consolidated CI, legacy recovery integration, route-source inventory regeneration and other concurrent files outside the exact maps are not granted a verdict by this bounded review. Prior UI review is separate; no all-controls-working claim is made.

The review digest must be installed only in the single normalized literal, then the complete registration/physical mutation suite must pass without review-dependent skips. Further mapped source changes require renewed independent review.
